title: The derivatives of `cumlogsumexp` are NaN after two leading `-∞` entries, also for finite outputs

found: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/1624 (closed 2019): `logaddexp(-inf, -inf)` was NaN. It concerns the value, which is right now, and not the derivative.

maybe_intended: The JAX FAQ documents NaN gradients where an intermediate value is not differentiable, as for `jnp.where`.
A maintainer could count this among them.
`jax.nn.logsumexp` avoids the NaN at the same input, which speaks against it.
description: After two leading `-∞` entries, the derivatives of `lax.cumlogsumexp` contain NaN:
the gradient of the last entry of `cumlogsumexp([-∞, -∞, 1])` is `[nan, nan, 1]`.
The NaN even reaches a function of a finite input with a finite result:
forward mode returns NaN for the derivative of `y ↦ cumlogsumexp([-∞, -∞, y])[-1]`, while reverse mode returns 1.
expected: `-∞` is the usual mask in log space, and `jax.nn.logsumexp` differentiates through it:
The last entry of `cumlogsumexp` is the same function, so it should have the same gradient.
And `y ↦ cumlogsumexp([-∞, -∞, y])[-1]` is the identity, so its derivative should be 1 in both modes.
reproducer: # The last entry of cumlogsumexp is logsumexp, which jax.nn differentiates through -inf.
# The gradient of cumlogsumexp is NaN at the -inf entries, also through jnp.logaddexp.accumulate.
# With the -inf entries as constants, the last entry is the identity of a finite input.
# Reverse mode is right, and forward mode returns NaN.
cause: differentiates `associative_scan` with `logaddexp`, whose custom JVP rule `_logaddexp_jvp` weights each tangent by
`_replace_inf` replaces only `+∞`. At `x1 = x2 = -∞` the result is `-∞`, so the weights are `exp(-∞ - -∞) = NaN`.
The scan combines the first two entries first, and the next `logaddexp` multiplies the NaN by the weight 0 of the `-∞`.
Reverse mode of the identity above is right because `grad` only transposes the path from `y`.
fix: In `_logaddexp_jvp`, give the weight 0 to an argument that is `-∞`,
as the derivative of the result with respect to it is 0 wherever the result is finite.
lean: Not modelled: the rule is `api.jvp` of `associative_scan`, and `logaddexp` is not a primitive.
